name: おにぎり浅草宿六 (Onigiri Asakusa Yadoroku)

claims.text: An English menu with photos is available, and the shop regularly serves foreign visitors, making it easier to identify and ask about individual fillings.

name: おすしあわせ 鮨ほり川 (Osushiawase Sushi Horikawa)

claims.text: As a small 6-seat open sushi counter with a single shared kitchen, there is no separation between regular preparation and any allergen-avoidance requests.

The restaurant will only attempt to avoid specific allergens or disliked ingredients if discussed with staff in advance, and states that full accommodation may not be possible if many ingredients need to be excluded.
The restaurant fries its panzerotti in domestically produced cottonseed oil, chosen by the owner for its quality and high vitamin E content, as opposed to more common frying oils.

name: らーめん ぽっぽっ屋 水道橋店 (Popposhi-ya Suidobashi-ten (Ramen Popposhiya)

claims.text: Noodles are custom wheat noodles (100% "Ocean" brand wheat) made by Asakusa Kaikarō; no gluten-free noodle substitute is offered.
The tare (seasoning base) is described as a sweet soy-sauce (shoyu) based sauce; no wheat-free soy sauce alternative was mentioned.
The broth is made by long-simmering pork leg bones (genkotsu) together with chicken (momiji) and vegetables — an animal-based stock with no vegetable-only broth option mentioned.

name: らぁ麺 はやし田 新宿本店 (Raamen Hayashida Shinjuku Honten)

claims.text: The shoyu (soy sauce) ramen's tare is a standard Japanese soy-sauce-based seasoning; conventional Japanese soy sauce contains wheat, and no wheat-free tamari or GF alternative was mentioned in any source.

name: らぁめん めん○（めんまる） (Raamen Men-maru)

claims.text: The broth is a clear soy-sauce (shoyu) base on a chicken-bone stock, made with standard wheat-based soy sauce and wheat noodles; no gluten-free alternative is mentioned in any available source.
Broth is chicken-bone (torigara) based and bowls come topped with pork chashu; no vegetarian or vegan broth option is mentioned in any available source.
The shop's broth is a shoyu (soy sauce) base; standard Japanese shoyu contains wheat, and no wheat-free soy sauce or GF alternative was mentioned in any source.

name: ラーメン二郎 新宿歌舞伎町店 (Ramen Jiro Shinjuku Kabukicho)

claims.text: The broth/tare is described as a tonkotsu-shoyu (pork-bone and soy-sauce) base; standard Japanese soy sauce is wheat-based, and no wheat-free tamari alternative is mentioned anywhere.
